title: Certified Minimax Risk for Cellwise Invitation Values under Weak Compliance
banked_reason: The note proves a narrow strict Gaussian contrast-information gap at two nearby profiles, an open-neighborhood extension, and a feasible pilot transfer, but it does not deliver the advertised published minimax-risk surface or meaningful frontier atlas.
gap_reasons: The finite games, correction terms, interval extensions, and joint-refinement algorithm are described only schematically, while no actual N_star, finite program, certificate file, rectangle list, or near-zero computation is supplied.

The claimed 32-rectangle atlas is obtained by arbitrarily subdividing one already-strict box, and the epsilon-frontier result is merely an existential cover of an equality set whose nonemptiness and geometry are never established.
proof_attempt_summary: The run reframed an inherited strict contrast-gap witness as a uniform minimax-enclosure and effective-frontier program, discharged its D0 proof graph, and verified the cited Raič convex-set theorem from the author's published PDF. D0.5 graded the delivered note incremental because no reproducible global enclosure certificates, resolution N_star, rectangle manifest, coverage audit, or substantive near-zero region were produced. A future retry can attempt the reviewer's finite computation program; the independent validity check found no impossibility proof, and the raw general-review receipt marked that program salvageable.
tldr: The causal target is the identified scaled invitation value \(\gamma_j=h\beta_j/2\), while \(\beta_j\) only parametrizes regret after division by unknown \(h\). The new headline is a uniformly certified minimax risk surface over \(\mathcal P_0=[1/4,3/4]^2\), not one favorable covariance profile. Finite randomized-rule primal programs and finite-prior dual programs, coupled with nonsingular cell coordinates, explicit Gaussian tails, parameter and observation discretization moduli, interval branch-and-bound, and outward-rounded probabilities, produce rational two-sided enclosures for both the cell and outcome-ITT contrast experiments with a published error tending uniformly to zero. Their monotone gap enclosures characterize the positive-gap set \(\mathcal S=\{\Delta>0\}\) and the zero-gap set \(\mathcal F=\{\Delta=0\}\), and generate certified strict and eta-near-zero rectangle atlases; the global geometry of \(\mathcal F\) remains open. The inherited \(0.267<0.2689966005\) certificate is retained only as a credited regression witness, and the split-pilot implementation remains a supporting upper-risk transfer under the same contrast-information contract.
gap: Gaussian treatment-rule and minimax-regret theory supplies limiting games, while the archived retry supplies only weak Blackwell ordering and the archived profiled computation supplies one strict point certificate. No cited result gives convergent two-sided minimax enclosures uniformly over a baseline-profile domain or an effective strict/equality frontier for the same identified invitation values.
fill: The project proves uniform rational enclosures with an explicit error sequence, monotonicizes them into exact set characterizations, publishes a nontrivial strict atlas and epsilon-frontier atlases, and retains the archived rule, prior, constants, and pilot transfer as reproducibility and implementation checks rather than headline claims.
